newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals demand low, prices steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals demand low, prices steady.

text.p: Indian base metals on Tuesday remained steady at improved levels, dealers said.
Demand from industrial consumers was low but limited arrivals and firm tendency in the world market kept offerings limited in the local market.
Volumes were dull as major players kept away, awaiting an announcement of the selling prices by state-owned as well as private producers for June, the dealers said.

Copper was steady at 13,625 rupees per quintal after gaining 25 rupees on Monday while zinc was quiet at 8,000 rupees and aluminium at 7,650 rupees per quintal. Both zinc and aluminium were up by 50 rupees per quintal on Monday.

Dealers said tin remained quiet at 31,400 rupees after gaining 200 rupees last week, while nickel consolidated gains at 37,200 rupees per quintal after a sharp rise of 400 rupees last week. Lead was steady at 4,150 rupees per quintal amid limited activity.
